title: Shelf-Life: confidentiality lifetimes of data categories
counting_convention: Years are counted from when the data is created or transmitted, the earliest moment a copy could be harvested. Where a law counts from a later event (death, account closure, end of treatment), the entry's reasoning states the conversion.

legal_retention_periods.summary: Clinical trial master file archived for at least 25 years after the end of the trial (subjects' medical files: national law).

entries.reasoning: EU law sets no confidentiality period for health data. The GDPR treats it as a special category (Art. 9) but stops applying at death (Recital 27); Member States extend protection after death (see the Germany entry). Harm from disclosure (discrimination, insurance, employment, stigma) lasts the patient's remaining lifetime and often affects relatives after death. Counting from the date the record is created: an adult patient's remaining lifetime of several decades plus a post-mortem margin gives 50 years at the low end; records about young patients reach about 100 years. Retention rules (e.g. 25 years for clinical trial master files) are shorter and are not a proxy for confidentiality.

legal_basis.quote_or_summary: 'data concerning health' means personal data related to the physical or mental health of a natural person, including the provision of health care services, which reveal information about his or her health status.

Processing of ... genetic data, biometric data for the purpose of uniquely identifying a natural person, data concerning health or data concerning a natural person's sex life or sexual orientation shall be prohibited. (Special categories; exceptions in Art. 9(2).)
This Regulation does not apply to the personal data of deceased persons. Member States may provide for rules regarding the processing of personal data of deceased persons.

Unless other Union law requires archiving for a longer period, the sponsor and the investigator shall archive the content of the clinical trial master file for at least 25 years after the end of the clinical trial. However, the medical files of subjects shall be archived in accordance with national law.

entries.reasoning: Genetic data is permanent, cannot be reissued, and reveals information about blood relatives, including children and grandchildren who were not born when it was collected. Its interpretive value grows as research advances. No jurisdiction reviewed sets a confidentiality period. The estimate covers the subject's remaining lifetime plus at least one following generation: 80 to 130 years from collection. The GDPR defines genetic data (Art. 4(13)) and treats it as a special category (Art. 9(1)), but does not set a duration.

Processing of ... genetic data, biometric data for the purpose of uniquely identifying a natural person, data concerning health or data concerning a natural person's sex life or sexual orientation shall be prohibited. (Special categories; exceptions in Art. 9(2).)
This Regulation does not apply to the personal data of deceased persons. Member States may provide for rules regarding the processing of personal data of deceased persons.

data_category.definition: Passwords, private keys, long-lived API and bearer tokens, key-encryption keys and other secrets that grant access to systems or decrypt other data.

jurisdiction.name: International / jurisdiction-neutral

entries.reasoning: No law sets a confidentiality period for credentials. Key-management guidance sets cryptoperiods: NIST SP 800-57 recommends about 1 to 3 years for private signature keys and no more than 2 years for authorization keys, and warns that if the data's required security life exceeds the cryptoperiod, protection must be reapplied. entries.hndl_notes: Special case. A harvested credential is only useful while it is still valid or still protects something; rotation shortens its shelf life.
